key_insight: Physics-constrained symbolic regression yields compact, interpretable relations for mean velocity and effective mixing length across zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers.
engineering_relevance: These relations could support engineering estimates of boundary-layer profiles while preserving key physical scaling behavior.
method: Start from classical logarithmic and Prandtl mixing-length scalings.
Identify near-wall transition functions under prescribed asymptotic constraints.
evidence_signal: The mean-velocity relation agrees well with 35 DNS, LES, and experimental profiles spanning friction Reynolds numbers of 252–72,526; the mixing-length relation captures principal trends in simulation-derived data.
watch_item: Applicability beyond incompressible zero-pressure-gradient boundary layers is not established by the reported evaluation.
paper_title: Physics-Constrained Symbolic Regression for Mean-Velocity and Mixing-Length Scaling in Zero-Pressure-Gradient Turbulent Boundary Layers
